Mathematics AB/ScB at Brown University

What Brown University asks of applicants to Mathematics AB/ScB for 2027 entry (the 2026–27 application cycle). Each requirement below is labelled verified, partly verified or not verified, with the date it was checked and a link to the official source.

US · All Brown University courses · Mathematics field guide

Entry requirements 2027 entry 7 of 8 verified
SAT / ACT
  • SAT or ACT required for first-year applicants (policy in place since the 2024–25 cycle); superscored
  • English proficiency tests do not replace the SAT
Verified19 Oct 2026Brown: Standardized Tests · Brown: International Applicants FAQ
English language
  • English proficiency test highly recommended for international applicants for whom English is not a first language, a primary language at home, or the primary language of instruction throughout secondary school
  • Accepted: TOEFL (incl. iBT Home Edition), IELTS (not IELTS Indicator), Duolingo English Test, Pearson Test of English, Cambridge English
  • Minimum scores expected in most cases:
    • TOEFL iBT 105 (before January 2026) or 5.5 (January 2026 and later)
    • IELTS 8.0
    • Duolingo 130
    • PTE 75
    • Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency 191

Brown says it “highly recommends” the test (not “requires”) and that the minimum scores are “expected in most cases”; it also states English proficiency must be achieved before admission.

Verified19 Oct 2026Brown: English Proficiency · Brown: Standardized Tests FAQ
Admissions tests

None listed on the official source

Verified19 Oct 2026Brown: Application Checklist for First-Year Applicants
Subject prerequisites
  • Not used in Altiora’s matching yet — see the note for the official guidance

Official: Brown has no specific course requirements for admission. It expects a minimum of four academically rigorous courses, preferably five, across core subjects each year, and recommends English 4 years; math 4 years, continuing through calculus when possible, particularly for students interested in STEM; science 3–4 years, including 2 years of lab science (biology, physics, chemistry when possible); history and social studies 3–4 years; world language 3–4 years. These are recommendations and apply to all applicants (Brown does not admit by concentration).

A-Level requirements
Grades
Not recorded
Details
Applicants should plan to sit GCE A-levels (where part of their curriculum) and submit predicted or actual scores as part of their credentials for admission; actual scores are expected before matriculation, and an offer may be rescinded if results do not meet predictions.
Verified19 Oct 2026Brown: Admission Criteria for International Applicants · Brown: International Applicants FAQ
IB requirements
Overall score
Not recorded
Details
Applicants should plan to sit International Baccalaureate examinations and submit predicted or actual scores as part of their credentials for admission; actual scores are expected before matriculation. IB scores do not replace the required SAT/ACT.
Verified19 Oct 2026Brown: Admission Criteria for International Applicants · Brown: Standardized Tests
Other qualifications
  • Advanced Placement: if you could not take the SAT or ACT, Brown encourages submitting other testing (AP, IB final or predicted scores, A-levels)
  • If your school requires AP or IB exams, matriculating students must share the results
Verified19 Oct 2026Brown: Standardized Tests FAQ · Brown: Preparing for Brown FAQ
Other requirements
  • Brown supplemental essays (via the Common Application) and two teacher recommendations required
  • Brown does not admit students by academic interest (concentration)
  • Personal video introduction (up to 90 seconds) encouraged; InitialView interview is one way to submit it for international students
  • Supplementary materials (music/visual art, research) optional
  • Considering a Bachelor of Science (ScB): at least one recommendation should come from a math or science teacher

Mathematics is offered as AB or ScB; the math/science-teacher recommendation applies if you are considering the ScB.
